title: Variance throttle: quickscan latency vs cost (annotated notes)
content:
Executive summary:

Quickscan of an internal experiment probing how short-duration request-rate variance (client-side burstiness + token-length skew) interacts with server-side throttle policies to produce non-linear latency and $$ per-query cost. This doc is an annotated lab notebook — rough charts, short tables, and open questions. Goal: decide whether to add a variance-aware throttle knob to Console (prefetch + soft-throttle combo).

Key findings (high-level):
- Small increases in short-window variance (requests/s 95th/mean ratio +30%) cause p99 latency to jump ~2-3x under current fixed-throttle policy, while cost per 1k qps increases ~12% due to inefficient slot packing and preempted batches.
- A soft-throttle (queue smoothing with micro-backoff) reduced p99 by ~35% in these scenarios and lowered cost by ~6%, at the expense of slightly higher p50.
- Tradeoffs depend strongly on client handshake timing jitter; worst-case patterns still cause tail events that require fallback capacity.

Methodology summary:
- Workload: synthetic conversational clients with 1–6 turn sequences. Token length mix: 20% short (<=32), 65% medium (33–128), 15% long (>128).
- Burst pattern: Poisson baseline w/ injected spike windows (10s) at 3x baseline every 120s; also a "staccato" pattern of 300ms microbursts for 30s windows.
- Configs compared: fixed-throttle (current), slotized batching (tiling), soft-throttle (queue smoothing + adaptive prefetch), and soft-throttle + prewarm.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1k-requests (in token-equivalent GPU ms), slot utilization, batch fill-rate, KV cache hit proxy.

Annotated results (text charts):

1) Latency percentiles during a single 10s spike (baseline 100 qps -> 300 qps):

Config      | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | notes
----------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | -----
fixed       | 48      | 320     | 720     | severe p99 jump, many preempts
slotized    | 62      | 210     | 380     | steadier tail, lower cost than fixed at peak
soft-throt  | 70      | 190     | 240     | best p99 vs cost in spike
soft+prewarm| 58      | 160     | 190     | prewarm reduces warm-start penalty

2) Cost (tokens-equivalent GPU-ms) over a 30m run with repeated spikes:

- fixed: 1.00x baseline cost (reference)
- slotized: 0.92x (better amortization in sustained parts)
- soft-throttle: 0.94x (saves on preemption, slightly higher idle)
- soft+prewarm: 1.03x (prewarm adds steady baseline cost, reduces tail)

3) Small ascii sparkline (p99 vs time, annotated):

Time (s):  0    60   120  180  240  300  360
fixed p99:  [__--___----^^^---------^^^]  (^^^ = spike peaks ~700ms)
soft p99:   [__--__---^--^----^---]      (peaks ~240ms)
slot p99:   [__--___-^-----^---]         (peaks ~380ms)
4) Batch fill-rate vs slot utilization (30s window, midpoint of spike):

- fixed: fill-rate 0.46, slot util 0.52 (lots of half-full batches)
- slotized: fill-rate 0.73, slot util 0.68
- soft-throt: fill-rate 0.61, slot util 0.64
- soft+prewarm: fill-rate 0.65, slot util 0.76

Notes / sticky threads:
- "Soft-throttle" is currently a prototype in runtime PR #662. Implementation detail: exponential backoff on enqueue delays + a sliding-window prefetch signal. We need an experiment to sweep backoff alpha and prefetch threshold.
- Open question: how will soft-throttle interact with client-side SDK retries? If SDKs aggressively retry short timeouts we create oscillation loops. Add a client backpressure header to SDKs? (see JIRA-ENG-1342)
- Observability: current telemetry lacks an obvious "enqueue-delay" histogram at the Console layer; we must instrument enqueue latency and batch preempt counts.

Operational recommendations (draft):
1) Short-term (A/B): roll out soft-throttle behind a toggle for 10% of traffic on Console dev region. Monitor p99, cost delta, and enqueue-delay histogram.
2) Medium-term: add an SDK advisory header for backoff recommendations and an auto-retry policy that respects server-suggested enqueue delay.
3) Longer-term: consider a variance-aware capacity planner that inflates warm pool budgets for tenants with high short-window variance (cost tradeoff analysis required).

Appendix: quick experiment checklist (for whoever picks this up)
- reproduce baseline Poisson + spike traces: run tracegen v2 with flags --staccato --spike-period 120 --spike-mult 3
- run PR-662 runtime image + metric-branch: instrument enqueue_delay_hist and batch_preempt_counter
- capture 30m runs, export to csv, produce percentiles & ascii sparkline with quick-spark.py

Open todo (notes to self):
- run alpha sweep on backoff parameter (0.1, 0.3, 0.6) and prefetch thresholds (10%, 25%, 50%)
- short writeup for Console UX team on how to present "soft-throttle" in rollout UI
- link to customer-impact case studies (we suspect mobile chat apps with quick-fire taps are most affected)

References and links: JIRA-ENG-1342, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/662, confluence:latency-cost-playbook, slack:#console-throttle

End of quickscan. This is a working notebook — plenty of rough edges. Ping me (Ethan) to sync and I'll hand off a formal bench report once sweep matrix completes.
